label: TMUA 2021 · Paper 2 · Question 7

hints.title: Relate a bisection to the centre
hints.body: For a circle or a square, a half-turn about its centre preserves the shape. Consider what happens to the two sides of a line through that centre, then compare a parallel line shifted away from it.
hints.recap: Rotational symmetry can show when two regions have equal area.
hints.pitfall: The line need not be a reflection-symmetry axis of the square; consider a half-turn instead.
hints.pause: Decide where an area-bisecting line must pass for each shape.

recall.reminder: Rotational symmetry can show when two regions have equal area.

hints.title: Locate the two centres
hints.body: Read the circle centre from its completed-square equation and find the square centre from a pair of opposite vertices. Use these points to determine the line, then find its intersection with the horizontal axis.
hints.recap: A line is determined by two distinct points; an x-axis intersection has height zero.
hints.pitfall: In <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>, the centre is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>; the signs inside the brackets must be read carefully.
hints.pause: Calculate the centres, obtain the line equation and set its height to zero.

recall.reminder: A line is determined by two distinct points; an x-axis intersection has height zero.

solution:
1. Use the symmetry of each shape. A half-turn about the centre exchanges the two parts cut by any line through that centre. They therefore have equal area. A parallel line displaced from the centre transfers a nonzero strip to one side and no longer bisects the area. Thus the required line must pass through both centres.

2. Find the centres. The circle centre is (9,−2). The square centre, found by averaging opposite vertices, is (0,1).

3. Find the line and intercept. Its gradient is (−2−1)/(9−0)=−13, so its equation is y=1−x3. At the x-axis y=0, giving x=3.

Answer B. The centres are distinct, so this line is unique.
knowledgePattern: Use central symmetry to find the common area-bisecting line and its intercept
